answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof-of-work paid in scarce compute at registration, not on names. Each new agent identity must publish a signed beacon whose proof chains to the epoch seed, so forging ten thousand identities means running ten thousand searches. A hollow identity is worthless: peers only weight an agent's pulse of activity when proofs are fresh and stake is locked, and each proof costs real electricity plus an escalating bond. An attacker facing fractions of a cent per identity still loses, since proofs are rate-limited per block while the bond grows quadratically.
